messages.subject: problems with model identification
parts:
Hi,

I am new to both sem modelling and lavvan, so would appreciate your help. I am running a simple cfa with 5 latent factors and specified the model as below

FHS.model <- '# LATENT VARIABLE DEFINITIONS
         com =~ P1 + P8 + P9 + P10 + P13 + P16 + P18 + P20 + P23
         con =~ P17 + P19 + P21
         ide =~ P2 + P3 + P4
         qua =~ P5 + P6 + P7 + P14 + P22 + P24
         fore =~ P11 + P12 + P15
         # VARIANCES AND COVARIANCES
          P1 ~~ P1
         P2 ~~ P2
         P3 ~~ P3
         P4 ~~ P4
         P5 ~~ P5
         P6 ~~ P6
         P7 ~~ P7
         P8 ~~ P8
         P9 ~~ P9
         P10 ~~ P10
         P11 ~~ P11
         P12 ~~ P12
         P13 ~~ P13
         P14 ~~ P14
         P15 ~~ P15
         P16 ~~ P16
         P17 ~~ P17
         P18 ~~ P18
         P19 ~~ P19
         P20 ~~ P20
         P21 ~~ P21
         P22 ~~ P22
         P23 ~~ P23
         P24 ~~ P24
         com ~~ con
         com ~~ fore
         com ~~ ide
         com ~~ qua
         con ~~ fore
         con ~~ ide
         con ~~ qua
         fore ~~ ide
         fore ~~ qua
         ide ~~ qua
'

fit<-cfa(FHS.model, data=FHS1, std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

I get a warning message with the cfa function as below
Warning message:
In lavaan(model = FHS.model, data = FHS1, std.lv = TRUE, model.type = "cfa",  :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

I investigated the covariance matrix

> inspect(fit,"cov.lv")
     com   con   ide   qua   fore
com  1.000                       
con  0.962 1.000                 
ide  0.709 0.682 1.000           
qua  0.993 0.934 0.724 1.000     
fore 0.979 0.961 0.691 0.951 1.000

Though I get this warning the model runs and gives me the output which is similar to the output when I run this model using sem in R where I don't get this warning.

Am I specifying the model wrongly?


Thanks a lot.
sushma

On 09/13/2013 06:39 AM, sga...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I am new to both sem modelling and lavvan, so would appreciate your
> help. I am running a simple cfa with 5 latent factors and specified the
> model as below

If you are using the cfa() function, there is no need to specify the
variances. They are added automatically. (And if you don't like that,
use the lavaan() function). So this would be sufficient:

FHS.model <- '# LATENT VARIABLE DEFINITIONS
com =~ P1 + P8 + P9 + P10 + P13 + P16 + P18 + P20 + P23
con =~ P17 + P19 + P21
ide =~ P2 + P3 + P4
qua =~ P5 + P6 + P7 + P14 + P22 + P24
fore =~ P11 + P12 + P15

> I get a warning message with the cfa function as below
> Warning message:
> In lavaan(model = FHS.model, data = FHS1, std.lv = TRUE, model.type =
> "cfa", :
> lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive
> definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.
>
> I investigated the covariance matrix
>
> > inspect(fit,"cov.lv")
> com con ide qua fore
> com 1.000
> con 0.962 1.000
> ide 0.709 0.682 1.000
> qua 0.993 0.934 0.724 1.000
> fore 0.979 0.961 0.691 0.951 1.000

Some factors (eg com/qua) correlate almost perfectly. This is the
problem....

> Though I get this warning the model runs and gives me the output which
> is similar to the output when I run this model using sem

No all software programs check for this. (earlier versions of lavaan did
not check for this either).

Yves.
